flashcards.q: Global vs regional scope of VPC objects?
flashcards.a: VPC is a global object spanning all regions. Subnets are regional CIDR blocks (with optional secondary ranges for GKE alias IPs). Routes are VPC-global. Firewall rules attach to the VPC, not subnets.

Stateful allow-or-deny, priority ordered (lowest wins), target = network tags or service accounts, source = ranges/tags/SAs. Implied rules: deny all ingress at priority 65534, allow all egress. Per-rule logging with sampling.

flashcards.q: IAM wiring that makes Shared VPC work?
flashcards.a: Host project owns networks/subnets/firewalls; service projects attach workloads. Deploying principals need roles/compute.networkUser on host-project subnets; GKE needs it for cluster AND node SAs. xpnAdmin attaches service projects to the host.

flashcards.q: Path of a request through a global external Application LB?
flashcards.a: DNS -> anycast VIP announced at every GFE/PoP -> nearest GFE terminates TLS -> Cloud Armor evaluates -> Cloud CDN cache check -> Premium backbone (cold-potato) -> regional Envoy proxies -> URL map -> healthy backends via zonal/serverless/hybrid NEGs. Failover without DNS changes.

Premium: enter/exit at PoP nearest user, ride Google backbone (cold-potato); required for global LBs, CDN, BYOIP, global IPv6. Standard: exit public internet at your region's peering (hot-potato), cheaper egress (~$0.085 vs ~$0.12/GB NA). Tier locked into reserved IPs.

flashcards.q: What do preconfigured WAF rules cover and how do you tune them?
flashcards.a: ModSecurity CRS-derived signature sets for OWASP Top 10: SQLi, XSS, LFI/RFI, RCE, scanners. Tune by sensitizing individual rulesets and running preview mode first to log would-deny matches before enforcement.

flashcards.q: Adaptive Protection - what does it do, and how do tiers differ?
flashcards.a: ML baselines per backend detect anomalous L7 traffic patterns and suggest WAF rules. Standard tier: alerting only. Enterprise (ex-Managed Protection Plus): full detection + suggested-rule auto-deploy option, Threat Intelligence lists, advanced network DDoS protection, hierarchical org/folder policies (GA Oct 2025).

Throttle caps requests per key below threshold while allowing the rest; rate-based ban blocks clients entirely for a configured interval once they breach a rate threshold. Keys can combine IP, headers, cookies, JWT claims.

flashcards.q: Dedicated vs Partner Interconnect vs HA VPN?
flashcards.a: Dedicated: physical 10/100Gbps circuits in Google colos, paired across domains for 99.99%-class SLA. Partner: provider fabric from ~50Mbps increments, no colo needed (~). HA VPN: IPsec over two tunnels/interfaces, 99.99% SLA, encrypted path.
Non-transitive by design: A-B and B-C does not give A-C route exchange. Need transitivity -> Network Connectivity Center hub-and-spoke. Each peering side administers independently; no shared IAM.

flashcards.q: Private Google Access vs Private Service Access?
flashcards.a: PGA: VMs without external IPs reach Google APIs over Google's network. PSA: dedicated CIDR allocated and peered so managed services (Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, Memorystore) get private IPs inside your address space. Independent features that coexist.

flashcards.q: How do pods get VPC-native addresses?
flashcards.a: VPC-native clusters allocate pod/service IPs from subnet secondary ranges (alias IPs): every pod routable in-VPC, visible to flow logs/firewalls, no overlay NAT. CIDR sizing matters - secondary ranges constrain node/pod counts.
